transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because people keep acting like I’m making it up, like I’m just getting worked up over nothing, but I’m not. My wife’s relative—he’s been coming into the house, getting at me. And everybody wants to dance around it.

I mean, my tools don’t just move by themselves. I’ve had those tools for years, I know where I put them. Same with my fishing stuff—every weekend, somehow, something gets spoiled or messed with, and then I’m supposed to believe it’s all just a coincidence. I used to fish with a guy from work, back when the plant had a different shift schedule, and we never had this kind of nonsense.

It’s been months now, and it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place, push me out. That’s why I’m here, because apparently I have to explain what’s right in front of everybody.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Voices? No, not like… I don’t sit there hearing somebody talking when nobody’s around, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that things happen and people act like I’m supposed to ignore it.

Like, I’ll be in the garage and I know where I left something, because I’ve had the same routine for years—work, come home, put things where they go—and then it’s not there. And then my wife says I must’ve moved it, but that’s just… no. But voices, no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
When these things happen, have you been drinking heavily?

Drinking heavily? I mean… no, I don’t think so. I’ll have a drink here and there, like anybody, but that’s not what this is about.

People keep trying to make it into something I’m doing wrong, you know? Like if they can point to a beer or something, then suddenly my tools didn’t get moved and my stuff didn’t get messed with. I worked in that plant for years, and you don’t keep a job like that if you’re stumbling around all the time. So… no, I haven’t noticed heavy drinking being part of it.
Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

Put thoughts in my mind? I don’t… I don’t think of it like that. My thoughts are my thoughts, as far as I can tell.

Now, people can get in your head in the sense that they keep pushing and pushing, you know? Like at work, back when I was on the line, a supervisor could say one little thing and it’d stick with you all day. But actually putting thoughts in there or taking them out—no, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I just know what’s happening around me, and that’s the part people keep trying to make fuzzy.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? I mean… not like a person standing there that nobody else sees, if that’s what you’re getting at. I don’t think so.

Sometimes you catch something out of the corner of your eye, but everybody does that, especially when you’re tired or when the light in the garage is bad. That fluorescent one flickers—been meaning to replace it, but then you go to the store and they don’t even carry the same kind anymore, everything’s changed over to those new bulbs. Anyway… no, I haven’t noticed seeing things other people couldn’t see.
About how long have you been convinced that your wife’s relative has been coming into the house and messing with your things?

About nine months, I’d say. It started right around when my wife’s relative moved into our home. That’s when I began noticing things weren’t where I left them, and you know, I’ve always been particular with my tools—when you work assembly, you learn to put things back the same way every time or the whole job gets messed up. But yeah… about nine months now.
Have you gone at least a month without drinking at all while this was going on?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I don’t keep a little calendar of it or anything. There were stretches where I wasn’t drinking, or not much, but a whole month with none at all… I’d have to think about that.

And see, that’s the thing, people ask it like it’s all neat, like you can just pull the receipt out of a drawer. But life isn’t like that. One week you’re working, then somebody’s schedule changes, then you’re fixing something in the house, and before you know it months are all run together. So… I don’t know for sure.
Have you heard voices talking to you or about you when no one else was there?

Voices? No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes you hear the TV from the other room and think somebody said your name, but that’s just the way sound carries in a house, especially with the vents and all that.

My hearing’s not what it used to be either, after years around machines, you know—presses, motors, that constant hum. But hearing people talking when nobody’s there… no, I haven’t noticed that.
Have people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Hard to follow? I don’t know… I mean, my wife says I “go on,” but she says that when she doesn’t want to listen, too. People at work used to understand me fine if it was about the job, because with assembly you have to explain things in order—part A, part B, torque this, check that.

Sometimes I’ll start explaining something and I have to back up because there’s a reason for it, you know? Like you can’t just say the wrench moved without saying where it was supposed to be, or what shelf, or who had been around. Otherwise people miss the whole point. So… I don’t know if they’d say hard to follow exactly. Maybe that I give too much detail.
Have you had any major medical or neurological illness, like a head injury, stroke, seizure, or brain problem?

I don’t know… major like that, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve bumped my head plenty of times, everybody has, especially around a shop. You stand up under something you forgot was there, or somebody leaves a cabinet door open, and then you’re mad for ten minutes because it was obvious somebody should’ve closed it.

But like hospital stuff, stroke or seizures or whatever… no one’s told me I had that. I haven’t had some big brain thing that I know of. Unless you mean something different by neurological.
Did this start during a time when you were drinking a lot or when you were cutting down after drinking heavily?

Drinking? I mean, I’ve had beers like anybody, after work especially, because when you’re standing all day and your back’s tight, sometimes you just want to sit down and not hear machinery in your head anymore. But “drinking a lot,” I don’t know what you mean by that exactly.

I can’t say I noticed it starting because of drinking or stopping drinking. It wasn’t like some weekend thing where I was on a bender and then Monday everything changed. People like to blame alcohol for things because it’s easy, you know—then they don’t have to look at what was actually going on. But as far as cutting down after drinking heavily… no, I don’t really have a thing like that to point to.
Has your wife’s relative ever done something to you that would be impossible in real life, like getting into your house without any normal way of entering?

Impossible? I don’t know why everybody goes straight to “impossible,” like that’s the point. I’m here because everyone keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative has been coming into this house to get at me.

My tools don’t move themselves. They’re where I leave them, because I’ve had the same habits for years—same bench, same drawers, same way of setting things down. And my fishing plans don’t get ruined by accident every single weekend, not like that. After all these months, it’s plain as day to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.

Now, how he’s getting in, I can’t stand there all day watching every door and window. But things don’t just happen on their own.
Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do things you used to do?

I don’t know. Interest comes and goes, doesn’t it? Like, you work all week putting parts together, the same motions over and over, and by the time Saturday comes you think you’re going to do all these things, but then you end up fixing something in the garage because a hinge is off or the mower won’t start.

I still do things when they need doing. Motivation… I mean, that’s a big word. Some days I don’t feel like dealing with anything, but who does? If you’re asking whether I just stopped caring about everything, I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to be?

Less expressive? I don’t think anyone’s said it like that to me. My wife says I get that “look” sometimes, but she says that about anything when she thinks I’m not listening.

I mean, I’m not one of those people who walks around grinning all day. At the plant, you keep your head down, do the job, don’t make a big show out of every feeling. My father was like that too—quiet guy, worked with his hands, didn’t talk unless there was a reason. So if my face is just my face, I don’t know what I’m supposed to say about it.

Voice-wise… I haven’t noticed anything. Nobody’s pulled me aside and said I sound different, if that’s what you mean.
During these nine months, was there ever a full month when you had nothing to drink at all?

A full month with nothing at all? I don’t know, I’d have to think about that. I’m not one of those people who marks every beer on a calendar.

Some weeks I might not have much, especially if work’s been rough or I’m tired, and then other times there’s something in the fridge because somebody brought it over or I picked it up after work. But a whole month, start to finish… I can’t say for sure. Months run together, you know? Especially when you’re working the same schedule all the time.
Before this started, were you drinking heavily most days?

Heavily most days… I don’t know what counts as heavily to you. I mean, some guys I worked with, they’d stop off every night and have a few like it was nothing, and then they’d still be up at five in the morning punching in on time.

Before all this, I had drinks here and there. After work sometimes, weekends sometimes. But “most days,” I’d have to really think. It wasn’t like I was writing it down. You come home, eat something, maybe sit in the garage, maybe there’s beer there, maybe not. It all kind of blends together when the weeks are the same. So I can’t say for sure, not the way you’re asking.
Has he ever done something to you that would be impossible in real life?

Impossible? I don’t know what you mean by impossible. If you mean like some kind of movie thing, no, I’m not saying that.

What I’m saying is real enough: he came into my house to get at me. Tools don’t just move on their own. My fishing plans don’t get ruined every single weekend by accident. And after months of this, you start seeing the pattern plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place, push me out like I don’t belong there anymore.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m making it up, but I’m the one living in that house.
Aside from moving or spoiling your things, has your wife’s relative done anything to you that would be impossible in real life?

Impossible, like… no, I’m not saying he flew through the wall or something. But people keep using that word to make it sound like I’m crazy.

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into that house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. And it’s funny, because I’ve had those tools arranged a certain way for years—ask anybody I worked with, I kept my station the same way too—and then suddenly things are off, missing, moved around.

So impossible? Maybe not impossible. But after all these months, it’s plain as day to me he’s trying to take over my place, push me out like I don’t belong there.
Was there ever a full month when you had nothing to drink at all while still believing your wife’s relative was coming into the house and messing with your things?

A full month? I don’t know… I couldn’t swear to that. I wasn’t keeping a calendar with checkmarks, you know?

There were stretches where I didn’t drink much, or maybe not at all for a bit, but then there’s holidays, weekends, someone comes by, or you have a beer after working on something in the garage. And honestly, when all this stuff with him started, I was more focused on what was happening in the house than on counting drinks.

So I can’t give you a clean yes or no on a whole month. I just know the things were still happening, or at least I was still seeing what was going on with my things.
Have you felt emotionally flat, like your feelings don’t show much on your face or in your voice?

Emotionally flat? I don’t know. I mean, I don’t sit around watching my own face, if that’s what you mean.

People used to say I was pretty even at work, didn’t get all dramatic about things. In assembly, you can’t be waving your arms around every time something goes wrong, you just fix the part, move the line along. But that doesn’t mean I don’t feel things. My wife will say I get a certain look, but she says a lot of things depending on who she’s been talking to.

So… I haven’t noticed my voice being flat or anything. I feel what I feel. I’m just not a big showy person.

patient.answer:
A full month with nothing at all? I don’t know, I’d have to think about that. I’m not one of those people who marks every beer on a calendar.

Some weeks I might not have much, especially if work’s been rough or I’m tired, and then other times there’s something in the fridge because somebody brought it over or I picked it up after work. But a whole month, start to finish… I can’t say for sure. Months run together, you know? Especially when you’re working the same schedule all the time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief arose in the context of a prolonged period of heavy alcohol use, to distinguish alcohol-induced psychotic disorder from primary delusional/schizophrenic disorders.
doctor.question: Before this started, were you drinking heavily most days?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about alcohol use before the symptoms began, but the provided symptom profile does not include substance use or drinking history.

patient.answer:
Heavily most days… I don’t know what counts as heavily to you. I mean, some guys I worked with, they’d stop off every night and have a few like it was nothing, and then they’d still be up at five in the morning punching in on time.

Before all this, I had drinks here and there. After work sometimes, weekends sometimes. But “most days,” I’d have to really think. It wasn’t like I was writing it down. You come home, eat something, maybe sit in the garage, maybe there’s beer there, maybe not. It all kind of blends together when the weeks are the same. So I can’t say for sure, not the way you’re asking.

doctor.question: Has he ever done something to you that would be impossible in real life?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the nature of the patient’s belief about the wife’s relative and whether it involves impossible events, which directly relates to the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
Impossible? I don’t know what you mean by impossible. If you mean like some kind of movie thing, no, I’m not saying that.

What I’m saying is real enough: he came into my house to get at me. Tools don’t just move on their own. My fishing plans don’t get ruined every single weekend by accident. And after months of this, you start seeing the pattern plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place, push me out like I don’t belong there anymore.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m making it up, but I’m the one living in that house.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is non-bizarre and circumscribed versus bizarre/first-rank psychotic, to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia or organic/alcohol-induced psychosis.
doctor.question: Aside from moving or spoiling your things, has your wife’s relative done anything to you that would be impossible in real life?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the patient’s beliefs about his wife’s relative, specifically whether they involve impossible or bizarre events, which directly concerns the delusional belief content.

patient.answer:
Impossible, like… no, I’m not saying he flew through the wall or something. But people keep using that word to make it sound like I’m crazy.

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into that house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. And it’s funny, because I’ve had those tools arranged a certain way for years—ask anybody I worked with, I kept my station the same way too—and then suddenly things are off, missing, moved around.

So impossible? Maybe not impossible. But after all these months, it’s plain as day to me he’s trying to take over my place, push me out like I don’t belong there.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a sustained period of complete abstinence from alcohol during which the delusional belief persisted, to distinguish alcohol-induced psychotic disorder from primary delusional/schizophrenic disorders.
doctor.question: Was there ever a full month when you had nothing to drink at all while still believing your wife’s relative was coming into the house and messing with your things?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the belief persisted during a month of complete alcohol abstinence, which relates to substance use as a possible cause; the provided symptom profile does not include alcohol or substance-related information.

patient.answer:
A full month? I don’t know… I couldn’t swear to that. I wasn’t keeping a calendar with checkmarks, you know?

There were stretches where I didn’t drink much, or maybe not at all for a bit, but then there’s holidays, weekends, someone comes by, or you have a beer after working on something in the garage. And honestly, when all this stuff with him started, I was more focused on what was happening in the house than on counting drinks.

So I can’t give you a clean yes or no on a whole month. I just know the things were still happening, or at least I was still seeing what was going on with my things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over persistent delusional disorder or substance/medical-induced psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you felt emotionally flat, like your feelings don’t show much on your face or in your voice?

target_item.reason: The question asks about emotionally flat affect or reduced facial/vocal emotional expression, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Emotionally flat? I don’t know. I mean, I don’t sit around watching my own face, if that’s what you mean.

People used to say I was pretty even at work, didn’t get all dramatic about things. In assembly, you can’t be waving your arms around every time something goes wrong, you just fix the part, move the line along. But that doesn’t mean I don’t feel things. My wife will say I get a certain look, but she says a lot of things depending on who she’s been talking to.

So… I haven’t noticed my voice being flat or anything. I feel what I feel. I’m just not a big showy person.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion focused on a specific person (wife’s relative entering the house, moving/spoiling belongings, trying to push him out) lasting about 9 months. He repeatedly denies hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, and impossible/bizarre phenomena. There is no clear evidence of disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or a medical/neurological cause. Alcohol-related psychosis cannot be confirmed because the delusion is not clearly tied to heavy use or withdrawal, and abstinence history is unclear. Overall this best fits persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
